Use computational methods to build, vary and communicate architectural form. Each assignment asks you to explain what your system does and demonstrate it through a clear result.

P1 establishes graphic standards. P2 is procedural: transformations, Boolean operations and ordered instructions. P3 is parametric: descriptive geometry, lists, reusable modules, repetition, conditions and attractors. P4 is generative: systematic field exploration, an architectural envelope and a fabricated contour model.

Use real architectural precedents for CSG and module construction. In 3.5, reuse the existing panel to design an architectural application with attractors. Use your Graphic Standards Manual throughout. Plain-language explanations, readable drawings and useful parameter values matter more than formal mathematical notation on assignment sheets. Explained mathematics remains in the lessons and presentations.

Project 4 develops one pavilion or small shop within a maximum 12 x 12 x 12 m envelope. All new required instruction ends by Week 12. The contour model is due in Week 13; the remaining classes support feedback, revisions and booklet preparation.

| Project | Approach | Assignments | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 — GSM | Graphic standards | Graphic Standards Manual | 5% |
| P2 — CSG | Procedural | CSG - an architectural object as instructions → 3D printing - from model to layers | 15% |
| P3 — Paneling | Parametric | Descriptive geometry - build a reusable module → Arrays - repetition, patterns and architecture → Attractors - three field studies → Attractor-based architectural application | 30% |
| P4 — Generative Architectural Envelope | Generative | Generative fields - a two-parameter matrix → Architectural envelope - pavilion or small shop → Contour model - registration and assembly | 35% |

Attractors are taught October 20. Submit the 3.4 studies and 3.5 architectural application together on October 27. Each subsequent class introduces the next assignment, due one week later.

October 27: submit 3.4-3.5 and begin the student-built 5 x 5 matrix (4.1). November 3: submit 4.1 and begin the pavilion or small-shop envelope (4.2). November 10: submit 4.2 and begin contour fabrication (4.3). November 17: bring the physical contour model to class and submit its fabrication sheet and files.

Digital submissions are due at 11:59 PM Eastern Time on each due date. All new required content ends November 10 (Week 12). November 17 begins feedback on the completed project; November 24 and December 1 support revisions, documentation and booklet preparation. No new graded assignment is due December 1. The booklet and revised GSM remain due at the December 10-16 final review; the exact review slot will be announced.

The recorded midterm deadline remains October 18 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time on Teams for 1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1 and 3.2. Review that work using the evidence already submitted; this schedule adds no retrospective deliverables or midterm assessment.

## Update and verify

```text
python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt
python scripts/sync_course.py
bundle exec jekyll build
python scripts/verify_course.py
```

Change the source first, then regenerate. Verification checks course drift, grading, dates, links, screenshots and publication paths. [GitHub Pages setup](reference/GITHUB-PAGES.md) explains the repository setting and checked deployments.

### Releasing a class

Classes, lessons and assignment briefs are published one at a time so students follow along rather than read ahead. The `release:` block in [syllabus/course.yml](syllabus/course.yml) is the switch: a page not listed there is not written to the site, and every link to it becomes plain text marked *not yet released*. The calendar, the lesson list and the assignment table still show every row with its date, so nothing looks missing.

The weekly move is one edit — add the week number, the unit ids and any newly briefed assignment, then regenerate:

```text
release:
  classes: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
  tutorials: [U01, U02, U03, U04]
  assignments: [P1, P2, P3, BOOK]
```

The current class and tutorial release is recorded in `release.note`. Review and update materials each week and update that note when advancing the release. Current assignment briefs for all four projects are available.

Assignments take the project id — listing `P1` posts GSM; `P2` posts both CSG briefs; `P3` posts the module, arrays and attractor briefs; `P4` posts the three final-project stages. The assignment overview page is always posted.

Use `all` on either line to publish everything. To preview the finished site locally without editing the source, run `SYNC_RELEASE=all python scripts/sync_course.py` — then run it again without the variable before committing, or the held-back pages go live.

Blender session files are listed once under `blender:` in the same source and linked from every lesson that uses them. A session is only linked when its `.blend` is actually present, and [files/blender/README.md](files/blender/README.md) is generated from the same list.

[Blender screenshots](images/blender/README.md) contains a Geometry Nodes and viewport pair for every session, plus a ZIP for preparing slides. The lesson pages and gallery follow the release list.

The site uses Jekyll and P2PU Course in a Box. Post filename dates control navigation order; actual class dates come from the curriculum source.

## Assignment brief structure and PDFs

Each brief follows Purpose, What you will learn, What to do, What to submit and What we assess. Keep useful dimensions and parameter values, but explain rules in ordinary language. The presentations may retain their explained mathematics.

Edit milestone requirements and brief fields in syllabus/course.yml. The same text generates the website and all four project PDFs. P1 covers GSM; P2 covers 2.1 CSG and 2.2 slicing/printing; P3 covers 3.1 module, 3.2.1–3.2.3 as one Arrays assignment, 3.4 formative attractor studies and 3.5 architectural application. P4 covers 4.1 student-built 5 x 5 matrix, 4.2 pavilion/shop envelope within 12 x 12 x 12 m and 4.3 registered contour model. The matrix uses instructor-supplied field tools; students construct the comparison themselves. Existing midterm records are retained. The weekly deadlines and 10/15/10 Project 4 allocation are current.

Run python scripts/sync_course.py to regenerate pages, README and PDFs together. The check mode also verifies source and PDF hashes in files/assignments/manifest.json. Commit the source, renderer, generated pages, PDFs, manifest and any retired-page deletions together after instructor review.

## Midterm grade

**Midterm deadline:** Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time.

The midterm grade accumulates the Graphic Standards Manual, CSG sheet and print, module (3.1) and arrays (3.2). These assignments account for 40% of the final course grade. Report the accumulated result as a percentage of those 40 possible course points. The midterm adds no separate assessment weight.

| Included work | Due | Course weight |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — Graphic Standards Manual | Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time | 5% |
| 2.1 — CSG - an architectural object as instructions | Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time | 10% |
| 2.2 — 3D printing - from model to layers | Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time | 5% |
| 3.1 — Descriptive geometry - build a reusable module | Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time | 10% |
| 3.2 — Arrays - repetition, patterns and architecture | Sun Oct 18, 11:59 PM Eastern Time | 10% |

**Calculation:** add each assignment's earned course points (assignment percentage / 100 x its course weight), then divide the total by 40 and multiply by 100. Use the course's existing submission and late-work policies.


## Assignment sequence

| Assignment | Presentation and files |
| --- | --- |
| 1 — Graphic Standards Manual | Four 17 x 11 inch pages in one PDF: template, typography, color/line styles and an applied sheet; editable layout and assets. |
| 2.1 — CSG - an architectural object as instructions | One 17 x 11 inch sheet: precedent, numbered diagrams/instructions and final view; editable model. |
| 2.2 — 3D printing - from model to layers | One CSG print; photograph and annotated slicer documentation PDF; editable geometry, print mesh and slicer settings/project. |
| 3.1 — Descriptive geometry - build a reusable module | One 17 x 11 inch sheet: panel precedent, three variations, indexed point/face lists and parameter table; editable module. |
| 3.2 — Arrays - repetition, patterns and architecture | Three 17 x 11 inch sheets in one PDF: four repetition diagrams, four conditional patterns and an architectural application; editable studies. |
| 3.4 — Attractors - three field studies | One study sheet with three attractor diagrams, included as page 1 of the 3.5 package; no separate upload or grade. |
| 3.5 — Attractor-based architectural application | Two 17 x 11 inch sheets in one PDF: 3.4 studies, then 3.5 elevation/isometric and comparison; editable studies and architectural model. |
| 4.1 — Generative fields - a two-parameter matrix | One 17 x 11 inch sheet: labeled 5 x 5 matrix, selected result and observations; editable matrix and supplied groups. |
| 4.2 — Architectural envelope - pavilion or small shop | One 17 x 11 inch sheet: plan, section, isometric, use/scale and design explanation; editable envelope. |
| 4.3 — Contour model - registration and assembly | One assembled contour model; one 17 x 11 inch fabrication sheet; separate full-size cutting file, editable source, part list and photographs. |

All four projects have concise PDF handouts. Existing presentations retain their explained mathematics; the revised briefs govern deliverables. The recorded midterm weights and deadline are unchanged; the weekly deadlines and revised Project 4 weight split are current.
